At 160 °C, it takes around 6 seconds to fully peel off the cathode from the aluminum foil. At the boiling point of ethylene glycol (198 °C), it takes around 2 seconds to fully peel off the cathode.

To calculate how many times faster delamination is at the boiling point of ethylene glycol than at 160 °C, we can divide the time it takes at 160 °C (6 seconds) by the time it takes at the boiling point (2 seconds):

6 seconds / 2 seconds = 3 times faster

So, delamination is 3 times faster at the boiling point of ethylene glycol than at 160 °C.
